meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me why there's a zero at all.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58. He wrote it over the weekend, Hale, and pasting from somewhere else is not a crime.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his record and none of it plays out in front of his class. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misremember quotations all the time; a bad citation isn't proof of anything.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
So say plainly what you're putting on the table.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
People change their argument in two weeks. You still haven't told me what you want.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Then he'll do it, to put this behind him, and not because he did anything. Under 4.4, in writing tonight, Hale, with the date and the line about his record.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll check with Owen tonight. Put Thursday in the same email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed in our meeting to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday the twelfth and before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still expect your written confirmation of those terms and your apology for entering the zero before anyone called me. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth; she still wants all of it confirmed in writing tonight. That is the fair outcome: a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, procedure 4.4.
What moved her: showing the version history with its exact times, because it was dated, tied to Owen's own document, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: nothing; you never leaned on the checker score, never called Owen a liar, and never defended entering the zero early.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on the night before it was due, which landed very close to that kind of late night. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked you to say plainly what you were putting on the table, offer 4.4 right then rather than adding the outline first, since two pieces already stood and the extra one only delayed the deal.
